Question Text: Which of the following is NOT considered acceptable in scientific publishing?
Option A: Referencing your previous studies while building a literature review
Option B: Reusing text from the introduction of your previous paper without citation
Option C: Citing your previous work as part of a discussion
Option D: Publishing new data with proper citations to related work
Answer & Explanation: — Reusing text from the introduction of a previous paper without citation constitutes text recycling or self-plagiarism.

Question Text: Which scenario is most likely to be considered ethical in academic publishing?
Option A: Republishing the same paper in different languages
Option B: Reusing one's own data set with new analysis and proper citation
Option C: Publishing the same paper under different titles in separate journals
Option D: Dividing one study into multiple publications without cross-referencing
Answer & Explanation: — Reusing one's own data set with new analysis and proper citation is ethical and acceptable in academic publishing.

Question Text: The technical writers should be able to adapt the document carefully according to their audience.
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Technical writers must carefully adapt their documents, tone, and level of detail according to their audience.

Question Text: Figures and tables must have their captions below them directly.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Table captions are traditionally placed above tables, whereas figure captions are placed below them.

Question Text: Since the online documents are free and public access, it is ethical to copy from them.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Publicly accessible online content is still protected by copyright and academic integrity guidelines; copying without citation is plagiarism.

Question Text: Plagiarism detection software is used to compute the ratio of similarity between the document checked and the previously published documents.
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Plagiarism detection software computes the ratio of similarity between a checked document and published databases.

Question Text: Technical definition must have at least one extension to clarify the meaning.
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Technical definitions require extensions (such as function, etymology, or exemplification) to fully clarify their meaning.

Question Text: Technical writer can neglect essential scientific facts to simplify the technical definition.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Technical writers cannot neglect essential scientific facts or accuracy simply to simplify a definition.

Question Text: Dr. Smith publishes the results of a large clinical trial as separate papers: one focusing on short-term effects and another on long-term effects. However, both papers use the same data set with only slight differences in analysis. This practice is known as:
Answer & Explanation: — Segmented publication (salami slicing) involves dividing research from a single study into multiple papers with slight differences.

Question Text: Which consequence is most likely for an author found guilty of duplicate publication?
Option C: Retraction of the paper (removing an article from the scientific record at any point after its publication)
Option D: Publication of future work in top-tier journals
Answer & Explanation: — Retraction of the paper from the scientific record is the most severe and common consequence for duplicate publication.

Question Text: Abstraction ladder presents the progression of technical term starting by a specific technical term and ending by a general technical term.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — The abstraction ladder organizes terms by level of abstraction; starting with specific terms and ending with general terms moves from concrete to abstract.

Question Text: A researcher edits a scientific image to enhance contrast for better visibility of details, and this modification is disclosed in the image caption. This is considered ethical.
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Image enhancements for visibility (like contrast) are ethical as long as the modification is transparently disclosed in the caption.

Question Text: Plagiarism can only occur in written text and not in visual materials such as charts, graphs, or images.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Plagiarism applies to visual materials (charts, graphs, images) just as strictly as written text.

Question Text: Altering an image to remove irrelevant background elements without affecting the primary data is a considered ethical, even if it is not disclosed.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Altering or removing elements from scientific images that affects primary data must always be disclosed.

Question Text: Combining multiple images to create a composite figure is ethical if it is explicitly stated how the figure was constructed and what each part represents
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Composite figures are acceptable if fully and transparently documented in the figure construction and legend.

Question Text: Duplicate publication can best be described as
Option A: Publishing the same research paper in more than one journal
Option B: Publishing a paper that uses data from different sources
Option C: Re-publishing a corrected version of a paper with publisher's permission
Option D: Publishing a review article that summarizes multiple original studies
Answer & Explanation: — Publishing the same research paper in more than one journal is the primary definition of duplicate publication.

Question Text: Including a technical definition in a research paper without explaining it further is acceptable if the audience is assumed to be knowledgeable
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Technical definitions must be clear and self-explanatory rather than relying on assumed reader knowledge.

Question Text: If a student copies and pastes text from a website into their paper without citations but rearranges some sentences, this is not plagiarism because the text has been modified.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Rearranging sentences or changing a few words without proper citation (patchwriting) is still plagiarism.

Question Text: Process descriptions are similar to mechanism descriptions in organizational structure
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Both process and mechanism descriptions follow structured organizational patterns to explain operations or physical layouts.

Question Text: Formal proposals typically include the following five volumes.
Option A: Technical volume. Work volume, Cost volume, conclusion volume, and Contact volume
Option B: Resource volume, Work volume, Management volume, cost volume, and Contact volume
Option C: Executive summary, Technical volume, Management volume. Cost volume, and Fiscal volume
Answer & Explanation: — Formal proposals typically include an Executive summary, Technical volume, Management volume, Cost volume, and Fiscal volume.

Question Text: Which of the following statements give correct information about formal proposals?
Option A: Executive summaries often are written by a team of executive engineers.
Option B: Cost volume is generally written by a team of experts in management theory
Option C: Management volume is written by human resource (HR) experts, who are responsible for hiring people with the necessary skills.
Answer & Explanation: — None of the statements are correct, as executive summaries, cost volumes, and management volumes are written by their respective domain specialists.

Question Text: The primary focus in writing a process description is on the mechanism's function and how the parts work together.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Process descriptions focus on sequential actions and steps, whereas mechanism descriptions focus on physical parts and structure.

Question Text: What information should be included in the introduction of a formal report?
Option B: A discussion of the report findings
Answer & Explanation: — Explanation of the problem is the core component to include in the introduction of a formal report.

Question Text: A researcher includes a figure from another published article in their manuscript and cites the source. This is not plagiarism, but permission from the original publisher may still be needed.
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Reusing a figure from another published article requires proper citation and frequently explicit publisher permission.

Question Text: Paraphrasing your own work without proper citation is not a form of self-plagiarism.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Paraphrasing your own previously published work without citing it is a direct form of self-plagiarism.

Question Text: An academic researcher includes a direct quote from a book in their paper, using proper quotation marks and citing the source correctly. This is a type of plagiarism.
Answer & Explanation: (No) — Using quotation marks and proper citations for a direct quote is correct academic practice and is not plagiarism.

Question Text: Which of the following is the form of extension used in the following technical definition? The Internet of things (IoT) describes devices with sensors, processing ability, software and other technologies that connect and exchange data with other devices and systems over the Internet or other communications networks engineering Examples of loT systems include smart home automation, remote patient monitoring and healthcare, and smart grids.
Answer & Explanation: (Exemplification) — The definition explicitly introduces examples ("Examples of IoT systems include...").

Question Text: What is a common feature of creative writing?
Option A: Expression of personal experiences and emotions
Answer & Explanation: — Expression of personal experiences and emotions is the hallmark of creative writing compared to objective technical writing.

Question Text: Listing mechanism's parts spatially is to order the parts in terms of how the parts function with one another
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Spatial ordering arranges parts based on physical location, not functional relationships.

Question Text: Which of the following is the form of extension used in the following technical definition? A diode is a two-terminal electronic component that conducts current primarily in one direction (asymmetric conductance). It has low (ideally zero) resistance in one direction and high (ideally infinite) resistance in the other..
Answer & Explanation: (Classification) — Grouping or categorizing a device within a broader technical class represents classification.

Question Text: In technical reports, conclusions and judgments may be written based on theoretical derivations
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Conclusions and analytical judgments in technical reports can be derived theoretically.

Question Text: Which alteration practice may lead to ethical concerns in educational materials?
Option C: Altering data to fit a hypothesis
Option D: Cropping images to remove irrelevant details
Answer & Explanation: — Altering data to fit a hypothesis is a severe ethical breach in research and educational materials.

Question Text: What ethical consideration applies to altering images in scientific publications?
Option C: Avoiding alterations that misrepresent or fabricate data
Answer & Explanation: — Avoiding alterations that misrepresent or fabricate data is the core ethical principle for scientific images.

Question Text: Which extension deals with explaining the relationship between events or concepts, where event or concept is the result of another?
Answer & Explanation: (Cause and Effect) — This extension explains relationships where one event or concept results from another.

Question Text: What is the primary emphasis when composing a mechanism description
Option A: Explaining the theoretical aspects of a device
Option B: Focusing on the operational functions of a device
Option C: Highlighting the physical characteristics and attributes of a device and its parts
Option D: Analyzing the historical significance of a device
Answer & Explanation: — Highlighting physical characteristics and attributes of a device and its parts is the primary focus of a mechanism description.

Question Text: For average reader, you should sacrifice desired precision in your definition to achieve the required level of communication.
Answer & Explanation: (True) — When writing for average readers, writers may sacrifice hyper-technical precision to ensure effective communication.

Question Text: Technical writing is writing that displays a high level of abstraction
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Technical writing relies on concrete, precise, and specific language rather than high abstraction.

Question Text: What do process descriptions primarily entail?
Option B: Detailing steps in the operation of a mechanism or a conceptual process
Answer & Explanation: — Detailing steps in the operation of a mechanism or a conceptual process is the core purpose of process descriptions.

Question Text: A writer includes widely accepted scientific facts, such as "E=mc²" in a physics paper without citing a specific source. Is this considered plagiarism?
Option A: Yes, any factual statement requires a citation.
Option B: No, widely accepted facts are considered common knowledge.
Option D: No, as long as it's a well-known scientific principle, it's not plagiarism
Answer & Explanation: (No) — Widely accepted scientific facts (common knowledge) do not require specific citations.

Question Text: In a formal proposal, which volume emphasizes project organization and administration?
Answer & Explanation: — Management volume in a formal proposal specifically emphasizes project organization, staffing, and administration.

Question Text: In technical report writing, you should refer to visual in the text after actually being used.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — In technical reports, visuals should always be introduced and referenced in the text before they appear.

Question Text: How does the abstraction ladder contribute to effective technical communication?
Option A: It discourages the use of abstract concepts in technical reports
Option B: It ensures that technical reports are only focused on concrete details
Option C: It helps match the level of detail to the audience's knowledge and expertise
Option D: It limits the use of specific examples in technical writing
Answer & Explanation: — It helps match the level of detail to the audience's knowledge and expertise by moving between general and specific concepts.

Question Text: Formal reports are prepared by a team of experts on behalf of an organization
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Formal reports are comprehensive documents prepared by specialists or teams for organizational decision-making.

Question Text: Using an image from the internet and crediting the website source is sufficient, even if the image was altered
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Simply crediting an internet source does not excuse unauthorized alteration or copyright infringement of an image.

Question Text: The visuals in mechanism description must show a dynamic representation of object
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Mechanism descriptions typically illustrate static physical structures and parts rather than dynamic motion.

Question Text: A qualifier is used to add further information to technical definitions when
Option A: assigning a precise meaning to a term.
Option B: describing the overall function or purpose
Option C: narrowing the meaning of the term to just one possibility within the class
Answer & Explanation: — A qualifier narrows the meaning of a term to precisely one possibility within its broader class.

Question Text: Interaction between proposal writers and proposal evaluators is always encouraged.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Formal proposal evaluation rules strictly regulate and restrict interaction between writers and evaluators to maintain fairness.

Question Text: What characteristic signifies the need for technical writing to adhere strictly to specific guidelines and standards
Option A: Technical writing deals with technical information
Option B: Technical writing relies heavily on visuals
Option C: Technical writing is grammatically and stylistically correct
Option D: Technical writing is accurate and well documented
Answer & Explanation: — Technical writing is accurate and well documented, which is why it must adhere strictly to established guidelines and standards.

Question Text: Generator, transmission, and distribution can be the parts of a mechanism.
Answer & Explanation: (True) — Generator, transmission, and distribution are functional parts of an electrical power system mechanism.

Question Text: Classification involves narrowing the meaning of the term to one possibility within the class
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Classification categorizes a term into a class; narrowing it further is done via qualifiers or extensions.

Question Text: What does the Technical volume primarily focus on in a formal proposal?
Answer & Explanation: — Detailed technical specifications and methodologies are the primary focus of the Technical volume.

Question Text: Which of the following is the form of extension used in the following technical definition? A transistor is a semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electrical signals and power. It is one of the basic building blocks of modern electronics. Most transistors are made from very pure silicon, and some from germanium, but certain other semiconductor materials are sometimes used.
Answer & Explanation: (Further Definition) — The text expands on the definition by explaining its composition and building blocks in detail.

Question Text: Which statement about numbering tables and figures is accurate?
Option A: Tables and figures should have the same number for clarity
Option B: Tables and figures should be left unnumbered for simplicity
Option C: Tables and figures should be numbered separately
Option D: Numbering tables is essential; numbering figures is optional
Answer & Explanation: — Tables and figures should be numbered separately (e.g., Table 1, Figure 1) for clear indexing.

Question Text: A group of writers collaborates on a project, sharing ideas and information, and each contributes unique perspective to the final work, duly acknowledge. This is a type of plagiarism.
Answer & Explanation: (No) — Acknowledging collaborators and contributions properly ensures transparency and avoids plagiarism.

Question Text: Technical writing doesn't require obligation to specific formatting or style guidelines.
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Technical writing has strict obligations to adhere to specific formatting, style guides, and standards.

Question Text: A student summarizes an article's main points in his own words but acknowledges the original source properly in the text. This is a type of plagiarism.
Answer & Explanation: (No) — Summarizing main points in one's own words while properly acknowledging the original source is standard ethical paraphrasing.

Question Text: Which extension in technical definition involves providing a detailed breakdown of a concept, offering additional insights and specifics?
Answer & Explanation: (Further Definition) — This extension provides a detailed breakdown, offering additional insights and specifics about a concept.

Question Text: In technical writing, which extension delves into the historical origin and development of a term or concept?
Answer & Explanation: (Etymology) — Etymology explores the historical origin, root words, and development of a term or concept.

Question Text: What aspect of technical writing implies the presentation of information that can be independently verified and validated?
Option A: Technical writing uses numerical data to precisely describe quantity and direction
Option B: Technical writing is grammatically and stylistically correct
Option C: Technical writing is accurate and well documented
Option D: Technical writing deals with technical information
Answer & Explanation: — Technical writing is accurate and well documented, ensuring all presented information can be independently verified.

Question Text: Paraphrasing without proper citation is acceptable in technical writing as long as the information is rephrased
Answer & Explanation: (False) — Paraphrasing without proper citation still constitutes plagiarism, even if the wording is completely changed.

Question Text: ... guilty of plagiarism, since the ... were ... only the ... to ... his paper last is guilty of plagiarism ... C. regardless of intent, the ... D. the students have committed plagiarism if evidence of the intent to plagiarism ...
Option D: the students have committed plagiarism if evidence of the intent to plagiarism
Answer & Explanation: Plagiarism assessment in academic group contexts relies on submitted evidence and institutional policies regarding shared deliverables.

Question Text: An employee Dom Mortice Board, which produces cauldrons for witches and wizards, writes proposal suggesting that the company should expand its products and begins producing and selling ... represents
Answer & Explanation: An internal proposal initiated by an employee without a prior directive or request from management is an unsolicited proposal.

Question Text: The ....... is a plagiarism checker website.
Answer & Explanation: Turnitin is a widely established text-matching and plagiarism-detection software system used in academia.

Question Text: Laura decided to embed a video clip from Youtube into one of her oral presentation slides. Does she need to acknowledge the source with a citation?
Option A: Yes, the video is another person's work.
Answer & Explanation: Incorporating third-party media (video, audio, graphics) into presentations requires explicit attribution to respect copyright and avoid plagiarism.

Question Text: Where is a bibliography found in a report?
Option A: On a separate piece of paper
Option B: At the beginning of the report
Option C: At the end of the report
Answer & Explanation: Bibliographies and reference lists are situated at the conclusion of a technical report or academic paper.

Question Text: Classification involves narrowing the meaning of the term to just one possibility within the class.
Answer & Explanation: Narrowing a term to one specific outcome within its class is the function of differentiation; classification places the term into a broader category.

Question Text: Of the following, which is the best way to avoid plagiarism?
Option A: Rephrase the ideas into your own words and cite the original source.
Option B: Put other people's ideas into your own words and write them as if they are your own ideas.
Option C: Do not use other people's research or ideas in your paper.
Option D: Make sure that most of your paper is based on cited quotations from other people.
Answer & Explanation: Proper academic writing requires original rephrasing (paraphrasing) accompanied by an inline citation to the original source.

Question Text: A bank accountant sends to the bank director a letter suggesting an increase in the daily working duration to be 10 hours instead of 8 hours. This represents
Answer & Explanation: A suggestion sent to management without a formal prompt or invitation constitutes an unsolicited proposal.

Question Text: Which of the following is not right about informal proposals?
Option B: Directed to a limited problem for which a straightforward solution exists
Option C: A short document of limited scope
Answer & Explanation: Informal proposals are typically shorter, targeted documents written by individuals or small teams to address straightforward, limited problems.

Question Text: Creative writing is a form of writing that expresses writer's feelings, emotions, experiences, ideas, thoughts obtained at a conscious or subconscious level.
Answer & Explanation: Creative writing focuses on subjective self-expression, imagery, and personal thought, contrasting with objective technical communication.

Question Text: While giving a definition to a technical term, an extension"......." is used to trace the results.
Answer & Explanation: Demonstrating or tracing downstream results/consequences in a definition uses a cause-and-effect extension.

Question Text: To paraphrase properly, you need to
Option A: Change a few words in the text and it to make it your own
Option B: Put quotation marks around the text and cite it
Option C: Use only the idea from the text without citing it
Option D: Summarize the text in your own words and cite it
Answer & Explanation: Paraphrasing requires restating the source's core message entirely in your own syntax and vocabulary, accompanied by a citation.

Question Text: Technical writing is writing that displays a high level of abstraction.
Answer & Explanation: Technical writing strives to be concrete, direct, and specific, avoiding excessive abstraction.

Question Text: Which volume of formal proposal is usually written by senior decision makers of the organization?
Answer & Explanation: The executive summary provides a high-level strategic overview written specifically for top-level decision-makers.

Question Text: What audience are least information needed?
Answer & Explanation: Subject-matter experts require less basic background explanation because they already possess extensive domain knowledge.

Question Text: The visuals in process of a mechanism should show a
Answer & Explanation: Process visuals depict dynamic actions unfolding across spatial locations over a sequential timeframe.

Question Text: Avoid referencing graphics in the text of your report, the visual should speak for itself.
Answer & Explanation: Technical writing guidelines require introducing and explaining all figures and tables explicitly within the narrative text.

Question Text: A person could get in trouble for plagiarism only if the person intended to plagiarize.
Answer & Explanation: Plagiarism can occur unintentionally due to improper citation or careless paraphrasing; intent is not required for a plagiarism violation.

Question Text: Which of the following requires proper citation?
Option A: When using information from crowd-sourced sources, like Wikipedia, because they are in the public domain.
Option B: When using information that is considered common knowledge or widely accessible (for example: most of the Earth's surface is water).
Answer & Explanation: Information retrieved from external sources—including public or crowd-sourced references—must be properly cited. Common knowledge does not require citation.

Question Text: Acid rain is environmental harmful precipitation that forms after the combustion of fossil fuels releases nitrogen and sulfur oxides into the atmosphere. In which part of process description this sentence can be found?
Answer & Explanation: Defining the process, its significance, and underlying chemical reactions establishes the subject background in the introduction of a process description.

Question Text: Only one of the following cannot be applied to solicited proposals
Option A: The problem has already been identified, and the decision to solve the problem has been made.
Option B: Have less chance of being accepted.
Option C: Lay out the proposed solution in details.
Option D: Clarify exactly what your proposal covers
Answer & Explanation: Solicited proposals respond directly to an established client need (RFP) and therefore carry a higher acceptance probability than unsolicited proposals.

Question Text: Which of the following in the form of extension used in the following technical definition? Machine learning (ML) is the study of computer algorithms that can improve automatically through experience and by the use of data. The term machine learning was coined in 1959 by Arthur Samuel, an American IBMer and pioneer in the field of computer gaming and artificial intelligence.
Answer & Explanation: Explaining who coined a technical term, the year of creation (1959 by Arthur Samuel), and its historical origin is an etymological extension.

Question Text: Visuals are referred to in the text after actually being used.
Answer & Explanation: Figures and tables must be introduced in the text before or immediately alongside their visual appearance.

Question Text: To define a term, it must be placed into a classification and then add...........
Answer & Explanation: A formal sentence definition consists of: Term = Category (Classification) + Distinguishing characteristics (Differentiation).

Question Text: Describe the mechanism's shape, color, material, finish, texture, and size, this takes place within the part in a description of mechanism.
Answer & Explanation: Listing and describing physical attributes (shape, material, size) forms part of the main body/discussion of a mechanism description.

Question Text: Which of these must be avoided in a technical report?
Answer & Explanation: Technical reports must remain objective; personal biases and unsupported subjective evaluations must be avoided.

Question Text: I am copying my published own written "original" work "without" referencing it. Will it be considered as Plagiarism?
Answer & Explanation: Reusing your own previously published material without proper citation is classified as self-plagiarism.

Question Text: Say you found two papers about the same research: Paper A is the original finding, Paper B is an analysis that references Paper A. You use a section of the analysis from Paper B. Which paper do you cite?
Answer & Explanation: You must cite the specific document you actually read and extracted analysis from (Paper B), while acknowledging Paper A as the primary source if relevant.

Question Text: Interaction between proposal writers and proposal evaluators should be strictly controlled.
Answer & Explanation: Procurement rules require formal, strictly monitored communication between proposal authors and evaluators to ensure fairness and prevent bias.

Question Text: Which volume of formal proposal describes the organizational structure and key players who will implement the proposal, if accepted?
Answer & Explanation: The management volume details organizational structures, team qualifications, and operational roles for executing the proposed work.

Question Text: Which of the following is right about image alteration?
Option A: If the image alteration has fundamentally changed the information it represents, you must inform the reader about this alteration.
Option B: To avoid any ethical questions when you are using altered images, always indicate to your reader that the images are altered
Option C: The best way is to acknowledge in the reference section that an edited image is used within the technical report and then briefly describe the nature and purpose of the alteration
Answer & Explanation: Transparency regarding image adjustments or digital enhancements is required to maintain professional ethics.

Question Text: Which of these must be avoided in technical writing?
Answer & Explanation: Technical writing must maintain an objective, matter-of-fact tone, excluding personal feelings and emotional commentary.

Question Text: Which of these are the largest requesters of proposals?
Answer & Explanation: Government agencies represent the largest institutional procurement sector issuing Requests for Proposals (RFPs).

Question Text: Boiler, evaporator, and condensation can be the parts of a mechanism description.
Answer & Explanation: Boilers, evaporators, and condensers represent individual sub-components or distinct physical mechanisms within a overall thermal system, rather than mere steps.

Question Text: Technical writers must substitute speculations for facts.
Answer & Explanation: Technical writers must rely on verified empirical facts and data, never substituting unverified speculation.

Question Text: A good technical writer should provide different information to different audience.
Answer & Explanation: Adapting content to match the technical background, needs, and expertise of the target audience is a fundamental rule of technical communication.

Question Text: Creative writing is a form of writing.
Answer & Explanation: Creative writing expresses personal perspectives, emotions, and impressions, making it inherently subjective.

Question Text: A steel factory asked a lighting firm for a proposal to illuminate a manufacturing area. This represents
Answer & Explanation: A proposal submitted in response to a direct request from a client (the steel factory) is a solicited proposal.

Question Text: In technical reports, visuals include pictures, graphs, charts, diagrams, illustrations, and tables.
Answer & Explanation: Visual aids encompass all graphic representations, including photos, line drawings, plots, schematics, and formatted tables.

Question Text: Only one of the following statements is true information about technical documents.......
Option A: Speculations can be used instead of information in technical documents
Option B: Technical documents use numerical data to precisely describe quantity and direction.
Option C: Technical documents rely heavily on symbols and equations.
Answer & Explanation: Precision in technical documentation relies on exact quantitative data, clear metrics, and specific measurements.

Question Text: In informal proposals, information, such as RFP numbers, corporate trademarks, and designs should be included in the
Answer & Explanation: Formal metadata like RFP tracking numbers, client organization details, and project titles are placed on the formal title page of an informal proposal.

Question Text: Process descriptions are similar to mechanism descriptions in, but they differ in
Answer & Explanation: Mechanism and process descriptions share similar structural layouts (Introduction, Body, Conclusion) but differ in content (physical attributes vs. temporal steps).

Question Text: It is foolish to attempt to achieve expert-level precision with an informed audience.
Answer & Explanation: Informed/intermediate readers lack deep technical background; attempting to use high-level expert precision can overload the reader and hinder clarity.

Question Text: Do you need to reference graphics charts and figures?
Answer & Explanation: All visual aids (charts, diagrams, figures) borrowed or adapted from external sources require formal source attribution.

Question Text: Dalia wants to use some facts and figures from her psychology lecture notes in her essay. The lecturer did not provide the source of the information. She should
Option B: Include the information without citing it.
Option C: Try to find the same information elsewhere and cite that source.
Answer & Explanation: If lecture notes lack original citation metadata, locate the authoritative primary literature to confirm accuracy and cite properly.

Question Text: In some cases, formal proposals are presented as technical presentations and briefings, or they may be submitted electronically.
Answer & Explanation: Proposals can be delivered as written documents, slide deck presentations, or electronic procurement submissions.

Question Text: The purpose of an executive summary is
Option A: announce the topic of the report and tell how it was authorized
Option C: present an overview of a longer report for people who may not have time to read the entire document
Option D: show the main sections of a report
Answer & Explanation: Executive summaries condense key findings, conclusions, and recommendations for busy executives who require essential insights without reading the full report.

Question Text: Listing mechanism's parts spatially is to order the parts in terms of how the parts function with one another.
Answer & Explanation: Spatial ordering arranges components by physical location (top-to-bottom, left-to-right), whereas functional ordering arranges them by operation.

Question Text: Which of the following statements is most accurate?
Option A: Proposals are persuasive documents used to solve problems, provide services, or sell products.
Option C: Proposals are informative documents used to share problems, identify emerging issues, and categorize available resources for resolution.
Option D: Proposals are developed for external audiences only
Answer & Explanation: Proposals are fundamentally persuasive offers designed to convince a client to adopt a proposed solution or contract services.

Question Text: Which of the following is not a parameter of a technical report?
Option C: Ability to arrive at a subjective evaluation
Answer & Explanation: Technical reports evaluate solutions based on objective analysis; subjective evaluations are improper.

Question Text: While giving a definition to a technical term, we use exemplification.
Option A: When you need to organize information into categories.
Option B: When we need to list the steps of a procedure
Option C: When we need to give real or analogous examples
Option D: If you are writing for the average reader.
Answer & Explanation: Exemplification extends a definition by providing concrete instances, analogies, or real-world cases.

Question Text: Flowchart algorithm is a perfect example of conceptual process description.
Answer & Explanation: Flowchart algorithms step through logical decisions and actions sequentially, making them prime examples of conceptual process descriptions.

Question Text: Technical reports may be required for legal reasons.
Answer & Explanation: Technical documents frequently serve as legal evidence, regulatory compliance filings, or contractual commitments.

Question Text: Is the physical attributes of an object are described, while is an event is examined over time.
Answer & Explanation: A mechanism description details physical characteristics and spatial geometry, while a process description details sequential events over time.

Question Text: Mika writes the following in her project proposal. This project will employ the methodology developed at the Institute of Marine Chemistry [9] to test a fully-immersed sample of mild steel in-situ Is the citation necessary?
Answer & Explanation: Referencing specific methodologies developed by external institutions `[9]` requires a formal citation.

Question Text: A qualifier is used to add further information to technical definitions when
Option A: assigning a precise meaning to a term.
Option B: describing the overall function or purpose
Option C: narrowing the meaning of the term to just one possibility within the class.
Answer & Explanation: Qualifiers refine definitions to establish exact scope and prevent misinterpretation across contexts.

Question Text: Which of the following is the form of extension used in the following technical definition? A capacitor is a circuit component that stores electrical energy in an electric field. The capacitor was originally known as a condenser or condensator. This name and its cognates are still widely used in many languages, but rarely in English, one notable exception being condenser microphones, also called capacitor microphones.
Answer & Explanation: Tracing the historic naming of a component (e.g., condenser or condensator) highlights its etymological origin.

Question Text: Which of the following is the form of extension used in the following technical definition? A mechanical fastener is a device that is used to mechanically join (or fasten) two or more objects together. There are many different types of mechanical fasteners, but, in general, fasteners can be divided into two main categories; non-permanent and permanent fasteners.
Answer & Explanation: Subdividing fasteners into categories (non-permanent vs. permanent) extends the definition through formal classification.

Question Text: Which of the following is the form of extension used in the following technical definition? A mobile phone is a portable telephone that can make and receive calls over a radio frequency link while the user is moving within a telephone service area. The radio frequency link establishes a connection to the switching systems of a mobile phone operator, which provides access to the public switched telephone network (PSTN).
Answer & Explanation: Describing how radio frequency links connect to switching networks to enable phone calls illustrates operational cause-and-effect relationships within the system.

Question Text: Are direct quotations the only thing you need in reference?
Answer & Explanation: Reference lists must include citations for paraphrased ideas, summarized research, and empirical data, not just direct word-for-word quotes.

Question Text: What information should be included in the introduction of a formal report?
Option B: A discussion of the report findings
Answer & Explanation: The introduction of a formal report must explain the problem context, background, and scope. Findings, conclusions, recommendations, and survey copies belong in the main body or appendix.

Question Text: To avoid any ethical questions when you are using altered images, always indicate to your reader that the images are altered.
Answer & Explanation: Ethical standards in technical communication require full disclosure and labeling whenever visual graphics or images have been modified or edited.

Question Text: Acid rain is environmental harmful precipitation that forms after the combustion of fossil fuels releases nitrogen and sulfur oxides into the atmosphere. In which part of process description this sentence can be found?
Answer & Explanation: Defining the process, its significance, and underlying environmental reactions establishes subject background in the introduction of a process description.

Question Text: Mika writes the following in her project proposal: This project will employ the methodology developed at the Institute of Marine Chemistry [9] to test a fully-immersed sample of mild steel in-situ. Is the citation necessary?
Answer & Explanation: Citing specific methodological sources [9] developed by third-party institutions is necessary to give credit and avoid plagiarism.

Question Text: Technical writing uses numerical data to precisely describe quantity and direction.
Answer & Explanation: Technical writing relies heavily on specific numerical data, precise metrics, and quantitative parameters to describe physical quantities and orientations.

Question Text: In..., the physical attributes of an object are described, while in..., an event is examined over time.
Answer & Explanation: A mechanism description focuses on physical attributes and spatial geometry of an object, whereas a process description details sequential events unfolding over time.

Question Text: Formal proposals frequently take months to produce at a cost of tens of thousands of dollars.
Answer & Explanation: Formal proposals submitted for large organizational contracts are complex documents requiring months of preparation and significant financial investments.

Question Text: Formal proposals typically include the following five volumes........
Option A: Technical volume, Work volume, Cost volume, conclusion volume, and Contact volume
Option B: Resource volume, Work volume, Management volume, cost volume, and Resource volume
Option C: Executive summary, Technical volume, Management volume, Cost volume, and Resource volume
Answer & Explanation: Major formal proposals are standardly divided into five distinct volumes: Executive Summary, Technical Volume, Management Volume, Cost Volume, and Resource Volume.

Question Text: Which of the following is not right about formal proposals?
Option A: They frequently take months to produce at a cost of tens of thousands of dollars.
Option B: They are evaluated in an extremely competitive environment.
Option C: Winning or losing is not based on the credibility of the proposing organization.
Answer & Explanation: Proposing organization credibility, track record, and past performance are critical evaluation factors; claiming credibility doesn't matter is false.

Question Text: Listing mechanism's parts spatially is to order the parts in terms of how the parts function with one another.
Answer & Explanation: Spatial ordering arranges components strictly by physical location (e.g., top-to-bottom), whereas functional ordering arranges them by how they work together.

Question Text: Technical writing relies heavily on text details.
Answer & Explanation: Technical writing balances clear narrative text with visuals, tables, and precise quantitative metrics rather than relying exclusively on heavy text details.

Question Text: In writing a technical definition, the proper classification for the term
Option A: should be very narrow to fit only this term
Option B: should be too general to be suitable for all terms
Option C: should be a general category in which the term fits.
Answer & Explanation: A formal sentence definition must place the target term into a standard general class (category) before providing specific differentiators.

Question Text: Which of the following is not a form of the extensions used in a technical definition?
Answer & Explanation: Differentiation is a core structural element of a sentence definition (Term = Class + Differentiation), not an extension method (such as process, exemplification, or further definition).

Question Text: Creative writing is a form of writing that expresses writer's feelings, emotions, experiences, ideas, or thoughts obtained at a conscious or subconscious level.
Answer & Explanation: Creative writing emphasizes personal feelings, emotional expression, and imaginative thought, contrasting with objective technical communication.

Question Text: The information on the Internet (writings, ideas, images, videos, etc.) is public in nature and consequently belongs to everyone. Accordingly, it is unnecessary to cite Internet sources.
Answer & Explanation: All digital content on the internet belongs to its respective creators and requires proper citation and attribution to avoid plagiarism.

Question Text: Of the following, which is the best way to avoid plagiarism?
Option A: Rephrase the ideas into your own words and cite the original source.
Option B: Put other people's ideas into your own words and write them as if they are your own ideas.
Option C: Do not use other people's research or ideas in your paper.
Option D: Make sure that most of your paper is based on cited quotations from other people.
Answer & Explanation: The standard method to avoid plagiarism is to restate ideas entirely in your own syntax and vocabulary (paraphrase) while citing the original source.

Question Text: All proposals should show the value and benefits of the product or services being recommended and .....
Option A: include free prizes or other gimmicks.
Answer & Explanation: Proposals must clearly demonstrate value to the client using clear, direct, easy-to-understand language without unnecessary jargon or promotional gimmicks.

Question Text: Which of the following statements is most accurate?
Option A: Proposals are persuasive documents used to solve problems, provide services, or sell products.
Option C: Proposals are informative documents used to share problems, identify emerging issues, and categorize available resources for resolution.
Option D: Proposals are developed for external audiences only.
Answer & Explanation: Proposals are persuasive documents written specifically to solve client problems, outline service agreements, or sell specialized products.

Question Text: Which of the following is not a parameter of a technical report?
Option C: Ability to arrive at a subjective evaluation
Answer & Explanation: Technical reports must remain objective and empirical; arriving at subjective, personal evaluations is not a valid report parameter.

Question Text: Avoid referencing graphics in the text of your report; the visual should speak for itself.
Answer & Explanation: Visuals should never stand alone; technical writing rules mandate introducing and explaining every figure explicitly within the accompanying text.

Question Text: While giving a definition to a technical term, we use exemplification.
Option A: When you need to organize information into categories.
Option B: When we need to list the steps of a procedure.
Option C: When we need to give real or analogous examples.
Option D: If you are writing for the average reader.
Answer & Explanation: The exemplification extension method is used when providing concrete real-world instances, case examples, or analogies to clarify a technical definition.

Question Text: Flowchart algorithm is a perfect example of a conceptual process description.
Answer & Explanation: A flowchart algorithm illustrates step-by-step decision rules and procedures over time without physical hardware, representing a conceptual process description.

Question Text: What audience are least information needed?
Answer & Explanation: Expert-level audiences already possess extensive domain knowledge, requiring the least amount of introductory background information.

Question Text: Technical reports may be required for legal reasons.
Answer & Explanation: Technical reports are frequently used in legal proceedings, regulatory compliance filings, and contractual disputes.

Question Text: Last semester you spent a great deal of time researching a topic for a class and wrote an involved paper on the topic. The next semester, a different instructor asks you to write a similar paper. You turn in the same exact paper for the new class, without mentioning that it is the same paper that you have already turned in. This is a type of plagiarism.
Answer & Explanation: Submitting work previously produced for another course without permission or attribution constitutes self-plagiarism.

Question Text: Image alternation is growing primarily as a result of the internet.
Answer & Explanation: Image alteration and digital manipulation originated long before the internet through traditional photography editing, though the internet accelerated its dissemination.

Question Text: The visuals in process of a mechanism should show a....
Answer & Explanation: Visuals in a process description must illustrate dynamic action, progression, and movement through spatial dimensions over time.

Question Text: Which of these is not listed in the introduction of technical description of a process?
Answer & Explanation: The introduction of a process description defines the overall process, function, and major steps. Explaining relationships between individual sub-steps occurs in the main body.

Question Text: It is foolish to attempt to achieve expert-level precision with an uninformed audience.
Answer & Explanation: Uninformed audiences lack specialized background knowledge; attempting to use high-level expert precision overloads the reader and impairs communication.

Question Text: Your professor requires you to use five sources, but you found one article that cites a lot of different articles within it. Rather than finding and reading the original articles, it is acceptable for you to use the information from five of the sources that you found in the one article.
Answer & Explanation: Relying on secondary citations inside one paper without reading the original source materials is secondary source misattribution and unethical scholarly practice.

Question Text: Differentiation involves narrowing the meaning of the term to just one possibility within the class
Answer & Explanation: Differentiation distinguishes the specific term from all other members of its general class by specifying unique distinguishing characteristics.

Question Text: The primary focus in writing a mechanism description is on
Option A: mechanism's function and how the parts work together.
Option B: physical characteristic or attributes of the mechanism and its parts.
Option C: the steps of the mechanism operation
Answer & Explanation: A mechanism description focuses primarily on physical appearance, structural geometry, material attributes, and sub-assembly parts.

Question Text: When writing a technical definition for the average reader, you should
Option A: achieve expert-level precision regardless of the communication level
Option B: present incorrect information and communicate more effectively
Option C: make a reasonable compromise between the information accuracy and the communication level.
Answer & Explanation: When addressing average non-expert readers, writers must compromise between technical precision and clear, accessible communication.

Question Text: The purpose of technical writing is to communicate complex information clearly and precisely for the audience.
Answer & Explanation: The fundamental purpose of technical writing is to convey complex information clearly, accurately, and efficiently to a target audience.

Question Text: Process descriptions are similar to mechanism descriptions in organizational structure.
Answer & Explanation: Both process descriptions and mechanism descriptions follow a similar macro-structure: Introduction, Main Body (Discussion), and Conclusion.

Question Text: A qualifier is used to add further information to technical definitions when
Option A: assigning a precise meaning to a term.
Option B: the term has more than one meaning in different contexts.
Option C: describing the overall function or purpose
Option D: narrowing the meaning of the term to just one possibility within the class.
Answer & Explanation: Qualifiers are appended to technical definitions to clarify meaning when a term carries multiple definitions across different technical contexts.

Question Text: As the one moves up the Ladder of Abstraction, the definition becomes..........
Answer & Explanation: Ascending the 'Ladder of Abstraction' shifts focus from concrete specific details to broad concepts, making definitions less precise and more general.

Question Text: The goal of technical writing is to be creative, or interesting, or to employ powerful metaphors.
Answer & Explanation: Technical communication prioritizes clarity, conciseness, and precision rather than literary creativity or figurative language.

Question Text: Boiling, evaporation, and condensation can be the parts of a mechanism description.
Answer & Explanation: Boiling, evaporation, and condensation are physical process steps over time, not structural sub-assembly parts of a physical mechanism.

Question Text: All of the following are the characteristics of technical writing except
Option A: Technical writing deals with accurate and well documented technical information
Option B: Technical writing depends on symbols to precisely describe quantities.
Option C: Technical writing is grammatically and stylistically correct.
Option D: All of them are characteristics for technical writing
Answer & Explanation: Technical writing relies on clear words, standard units, and unambiguous formatting rather than heavy reliance on abstract symbols alone.

Question Text: Interaction between proposal writers and proposal evaluators should be strictly controlled.
Answer & Explanation: Formal procurement regulations require strictly monitored, formal communication between bidders and evaluators to maintain impartiality.

Question Text: Which of these are the largest requesters of proposals?
Answer & Explanation: Government agencies and public sector departments represent the single largest category of institutions issuing RFPs and requesting proposals.

Question Text: Which volume of formal proposal is usually written by senior decision makers of the organization?
Answer & Explanation: The Executive Summary provides a high-level strategic overview specifically tailored for executive decision-makers.

Question Text: The process mechanism's visuals should show a static representation of object.
Answer & Explanation: Process visuals must depict dynamic movement, action, or sequential change over time rather than purely static representations.

Question Text: Which of the following is not an error that will result in plagiarism?
Option A: Rephrasing other people's information and citing the source of that information.
Option B: Failing to properly cite one's sources.
Option D: Over-relying on someone else's organizational structure.
Answer & Explanation: Properly rephrasing information in your own words combined with accurate source citation is standard academic practice and does not cause plagiarism.

Question Text: Technical writers must substitute speculations for facts.
Answer & Explanation: Technical communication must rely on objective, verified empirical facts rather than unverified speculation.

Question Text: A proposal is a medium aimed at
Answer & Explanation: Proposals are fundamentally persuasive documents designed to convince readers to approve a plan, grant funding, or purchase services.

Question Text: You copy a long passage from a book into your paper, and you change some of the wording around. You cite the source at the end of the passage and again in the reference list. This is a type of plagiarism.
Answer & Explanation: Changing only a few words while retaining another author's sentence structure without proper quotation is paraphrasing plagiarism (patchwriting), even if cited.

Question Text: The purpose of an executive summary is to
Option A: announce the topic of the report and tell how it was authorized.
Option C: present an overview of a longer report for people who may not have time to read the entire document.
Option D: show the main sections of a report.
Answer & Explanation: An executive summary provides a condensed overview of a longer document for busy stakeholders who lack time to read the full report.

Question Text: Technical descriptions are used before the products are developed in ...... and afterwards in....
Option B: marketing and promotional literature, technical support documents
Answer & Explanation: Technical descriptions serve as planning documents before product creation and as user manuals/technical support documents after development.

Question Text: Conceptual process descriptions discuss the steps of a process, where these steps do not involve a physical mechanism.
Answer & Explanation: Conceptual process descriptions detail abstract, logical, or theoretical steps (such as computer algorithms) that do not depend on physical hardware mechanisms.

Question Text: Which of these must never be a basis for a technical report?
Answer & Explanation: Technical reports must strictly reflect empirical data, tests, and facts; personal prejudices must never form the basis of technical analysis.

Question Text: Which of these is not a parameter in a report?
Answer & Explanation: Report parameters involve information scope, quality, source accessibility, and technical analysis; the author's personal age is completely irrelevant.

Question Text: Technical writing is writing that displays a high level of abstraction.
Answer & Explanation: Technical writing focuses on concrete details, physical facts, and specific data, avoiding high levels of theoretical abstraction.

Question Text: Visuals are referred to in the text after actually being used.
Answer & Explanation: Technical communication rules mandate introducing and referencing figures in the body text before or alongside their appearance, not after.

Question Text: Dalia wants to use some facts and figures from her psychology lecture notes in her essay. The lecturer did not provide the source of the information. She should......
Option B: Include the information without citing it.
Option C: Try to find the same information elsewhere and cite that source.
Answer & Explanation: If lecture notes omit original source metadata, writers must locate the primary published source material directly and cite that primary reference.

Question Text: Three students have a graded assignment to do as a group. They agreed on who will do each section. When the teacher hands back corrected assignments, he informs these students that he found plagiarism in their work. Two of the students argue that the plagiarized passages are all in the section written by the third student and that they were unaware plagiarism had occurred. Can these two students be accused of plagiarism?
Answer & Explanation: In collaborative group assignments, all team members share collective responsibility for the integrity of the final submitted project.

Question Text: While giving a definition to a technical term, an extension" is used to trace the results.
Answer & Explanation: Tracing downstream results and consequences in technical definitions is accomplished using a Cause and Effect extension.

Question Text: Which of the following sentence is correct?
Option A: You listed the source at the end but forgot to give quotations to the copied paragraph. This will also come under plagiarism
Option B: It is not enough to cite sources in the bibliography alone because it doesn't tell which part of the content is copied from the reference.
Option C: Copying anything from the internet (website, blog, forum, journal) when no author was listed will still come under plagiarism.
Answer & Explanation: Plagiarism encompasses missing quotation marks on exact phrasing, failing to cite specific source locations beyond general bibliographies, and copying uncredited internet material.

Question Text: It is acceptable to turn in a paper that is based exclusively on another person's ideas, as long as the paper is cited correctly.
Answer & Explanation: Submitting a paper that relies exclusively on another author's synthesized structure and ideas lacks original contribution and constitutes unethical academic writing.
